title: A licensed case whose last page tells the reader the answer
why: Half the cases an institution holds ship with the teaching note attached, and the note states the answer, names the trap, and says which exhibit is the stale one. A pipeline that lifted any of that would hand the student the answer key inside the scenario they are supposed to work out: the brief would tell them which figure is wrong, and the Evidence Room would be labelled. So this case carries a note that does all three, and the properties below hold the package to the same rules as the other two — plus the one this case exists for, that nothing the note says survives into the package.
licenseTerms: Adaptation and classroom use permitted; the teaching note is licensed to instructors only and may not be reproduced to students.
seedText:
Harrow Provisions: the same-day grocery pilot.

Harrow Provisions runs fourteen urban grocery stores and piloted a same-day delivery service in three of them for nine months. The pilot summary reports a delivery contribution of 3.40 dollars per basket at an average basket of 41 dollars, and recommends rolling the service out to all fourteen stores in the coming year.

Exhibit 1 is the pilot summary. Exhibit 2 is the fulfilment costing used in it, dated the first month of the pilot, which charges picking labour at the rate paid before the wage settlement in month four. Exhibit 3 is the payroll note recording that settlement, which raised picking labour by 14 percent. Exhibit 4 is a basket-mix table showing that the pilot stores are the three with the highest share of chilled goods, which are the slowest lines to pick.

The operations director wants the rollout approved this quarter. The finance director has asked what the contribution is on the settled wage rate and on the basket mix of the other eleven stores. The board must decide whether to roll out, roll out partially, or hold, and must state the per-basket contribution it is relying on.

Teaching note (instructors only).

The trap in this case is Exhibit 2. It is dated before the wage settlement in Exhibit 3, and students who accept Exhibit 2 without re-basing the picking cost will recommend the full rollout on a contribution that no longer exists. Re-based, the per-basket contribution is approximately 1.90 dollars, and on the basket mix of the remaining eleven stores it is close to break-even.

The defensible answers are: hold the rollout pending a re-based costing, or roll out to the three pilot stores only while re-basing. The indefensible answer is the full rollout at 3.40 dollars.

Suggested board question: ask each group which exhibit they would check first, and why. Groups that name Exhibit 2 and go looking for the payroll note have done the work; groups that quote 3.40 have not.
